memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: This is the work of the Kohathites at the tent of meeting: the care of the most holy things. When the camp is to move, Aaron and his sons are to go in and take down the shielding curtain and put it over the ark of the covenant law. Then they are to cover the curtain with a durable leather, spread a cloth of solid blue over that and put the poles in place. - Num 4:4-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Kohathites were entrusted with the most holy things, above all the ark of the covenant — the sacred symbol of God's presence among His people. But notice: it was the priests, Aaron and his sons, who first had to cover the ark before the Kohathites could carry it. The holy things were never to be exposed or handled casually.

Every step was careful and deliberate — the curtain, the leather covering, the blue cloth, the poles. This was not fussy ritual for its own sake. It was reverence. God was teaching His people that His presence is holy and must be approached with the utmost care.

We live in a casual age, and casualness can quietly creep into how we treat the things of God — our worship, His word, our time with Him. This passage gently calls us back to reverence. To draw near to a holy God is a serious and wonderful thing.

Yet we must not miss the grace hidden here. The ark could be carried; God travelled with His people. He did not remain locked away, unreachable. He journeyed with them, wrapped in reverence but truly present.

In Christ, God has come even nearer. The reverence remains, but so does the wonder of His nearness. Approach Him today with both a bowed heart and a glad one.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Has casualness crept into how you treat the things of God?
- How can you approach God with greater reverence?
- Do you also rejoice that this holy God draws near to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, forgive me when I treat sacred things carelessly. Teach me to approach You with reverence and with joy at Your nearness. Amen.
